report:
Reviewed the complete keyed_reuse claim, ordinary external_trait_signature association, explicit provider_fact_reuse TODO implementation region, and sole metadata_keyed_reuse TODO test. Captured the metadata design and accepted provider-fact RFD. Source inspection only; no test execution or source changes.

The claim requires each lowered fact to observe only its corresponding owned provider fact, unchanged requests to reuse lowered values without new raw requests, and unrelated provider changes not to invalidate that value. The ordinary implementation is a Salsa-tracked external_trait_signature query keyed by SymExt, requesting the raw trait signature via crate number/definition index and lowering it into owned semantic storage. Neighboring tracked queries similarly separate products and associated-value requests carry impl and associated-definition identities. This is current lowering-level memoization, not an implemented independently tracked provider-input layer.

The explicit TODO accurately identifies the missing prerequisite: definition/product-keyed owned provider inputs with per-fact invalidation wired into each lowered query. It also records a concrete remaining dependency mismatch visible in the same source: lower_associated_type_value fetches external_impl_signature to obtain binder generics in addition to its raw associated-value input. A self-contained associated-value provider fact must supply the necessary binder information before the one-corresponding-fact requirement is fulfilled. I do not interpret current immutable-service memoization as proof of relevant/unrelated provider-edit behavior or silently accept that extra fact as satisfying the complete claim.

The metadata_keyed_reuse test is TODO and contains no assertions. It requires cold/warm query-to-raw-operation pairing, no repeat execution on warm requests, relevant edit invalidation and unrelated-key preservation/backdating. Completing the provider representation and associated binder ownership is explicitly prerequisite to that verification matrix. The RFD's narrow provider fact boundary supports that destination but is not runtime evidence. Both implementation entries and the test are accounted for; current partial memoization and the full missing provider/update behavior remain distinguished. The documented implementation and evidence deferrals are honest and concrete, so no additional edits are requested.
